# Background & aims

1.  

## Literature

- Cornwell & Ackerly 2009
- Ogle 2014 - wood density
- Fischer et al 2025 (in review) - Global Wood Density Database. partition variance at different levels of biological organisation and with and quantify correlations with climate variables. They fit exactly the same structure for the mixed effect model that I ended up using, including the two climate variables, the average species value and the centered deviation from the average. Reassuring that they converged on the same approach. They cite an Gelman reference (guru statistician) where they recommend this approach for LMMs when "Predictors and Group Effects Correlate"  https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.1010095

```{r}
# δ13C transformation follows Cernusak & Ubierna:
# Carbon Isotope Effects in Relation to CO2 Assimilation by Tree Canopies
# https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-92698-4_9

data_traits_climate <-  data_traits_climate_raw |>
  # Drop photosynthetic_pathway rows (categorical, not a modelled trait)
  filter(trait_name %in% c("huber_value","leaf_N_per_area","leaf_area","leaf_delta13C","leaf_mass_per_area","wood_density","seed_dry_mass")) |>
  # Extract collection year from date strings; average if a range is given
  # NOTE: year / delta13c_a are computed for all rows but only used for leaf_delta13C
  mutate(year = map_dbl(collection_date, function(d) {
    years <- as.numeric(unlist(regmatches(d, gregexpr("\\d{4}", d))))
    if (length(years) > 1) round(mean(years)) else years[1]
  })) |>
  # Estimate atmospheric δ13C at time of collection using a linear time trend
  mutate(delta13c_a = 39.7336 - 0.0239*year) |>
  # Step 1: convert raw leaf δ13C (‰) to isotope discrimination Δ (‰)
  #   Δ = (δ_atm - δ_leaf) / (1 + δ_leaf/1000)
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C",(delta13c_a- value) / (1+(value/1000)), value)) |>
  # Step 2: convert Δ to ci/ca ratio (proxy for intrinsic WUE)
  #   ci/ca = (Δ - a) / (b - a)  where a = 4.4‰ (diffusion), b = 27‰ (carboxylation)
  #   Higher ci/ca → lower WUE
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "huber_value",value*1e2, value)) |>
  mutate(value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C",(value - 4.4)/(27-4.4), value)) |>
  drop_na(value) |>
  # NOTE: range-based select relies on column ordering from the parquet file;
  # 'cell' must fall between decimal_longitude and life_stage for ncell to work below
  select(decimal_longitude:life_stage, woody)
  
data_traits_climate <- data_traits_climate |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log(annual_precipitation),
    # leaf_delta13C is already on a bounded (0-1) ci/ca scale; log-transform all other traits
    log_value = ifelse(trait_name == "leaf_delta13C", value, log(value))
  ) |>
  # Count how many unique climate cells each species appears in (across ALL traits)
  group_by(taxon_name, trait_name) |>
  mutate(ncell = length(unique((cell)))) |> 
  ungroup() |>
  # Require species to appear in at least 2 climate cells (needed to estimate intraspecific variation)
    filter(ncell > 1) |>
  # 3 required for convergence in huber value
    # filter(!(trait_name == "huber_value" & ncell < 3)) |>
  # Remove pteridophytes / lycophytes (too few observations for reliable estimates)
  # huber_value and wood_density are only meaningful for woody species
  filter(!(trait_name %in% c("wood_density", "huber_value") & woody != "woody"))
```

```{r}
# --- Step B: Compute global scaling parameters for climate variables ---
# distinct(cell) ensures each climate cell is weighted equally regardless of how
# many species observations it has (otherwise high-diversity cells would dominate).
# These scalers are applied to all traits combined (union of all cells, not per-trait).
log_annual_precipitation_scaler <- data_traits_climate %>%
  distinct(cell,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(log_annual_precipitation) %>%
  scale()

log_annual_precipitation_scaler_center <- attr(log_annual_precipitation_scaler, "scaled:center")

log_annual_precipitation_scaler_scale <- attr(log_annual_precipitation_scaler, "scaled:scale")

average_temperature_scaler <- data_traits_climate %>%
  distinct(cell,.keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pull(average_temperature)%>%
  scale()

average_temperature_scaler_center <- attr(average_temperature_scaler, "scaled:center")

average_temperature_scaler_scale <- attr(average_temperature_scaler, "scaled:scale")

data_traits_climate |>
  # --- Step C: Standardise climate variables (z-score, cell-weighted) ---
  mutate(std_log_annual_precipitation = (log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_scaler_center)/log_annual_precipitation_scaler_scale,
         std_average_temperature = (average_temperature - average_temperature_scaler_center)/average_temperature_scaler_scale) |>
  # --- Step D: Extract one climate value per (species × cell) combination ---
  # Nest so that each row represents one unique cell a species occupies.
  # [1] is safe here because log_annual_precipitation / average_temperature are
  # raster-derived and identical for all observations within the same cell.
  group_by(taxon_name, cell) |>
  nest() |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$log_annual_precipitation[1]),
    average_temperature_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$average_temperature[1]),
    std_log_annual_precipitation_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$std_log_annual_precipitation[1]),
    std_average_temperature_cell = map_dbl(data, ~.x$std_average_temperature[1])
  ) |>
  # --- Step E: Compute each species' mean climate position ---
  # The mean is taken over all cells the species occupies across ALL traits jointly.
  # A species' mean climate position is therefore the same for all its traits.
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(log_annual_precipitation_cell),
    average_temperature_mn = mean(average_temperature_cell)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    std_log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(std_log_annual_precipitation_cell),
    std_average_temperature_mn = mean(std_average_temperature_cell)
  ) |>
  # --- Step F: Restore individual observations and compute intraspecific deviations ---
  # Each observation's climate position minus its species' mean climate position.
  # This within-species deviation is the intraspecific (plasticity) component used in models.
  unnest(data) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn,
    std_log_annual_precipitation_c = std_log_annual_precipitation - std_log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    std_average_temperature_c = std_average_temperature - std_average_temperature_mn) -> data_traits_climate
```

```{r}
traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)

# Helper: extract fixed effects from a frequentist glmmTMB model.
# Returns a tidy tibble with z-statistic and p-value columns.
extract_freq_fixed <- function(fit, climate_var, trait) {
  tidy(fit, effects = "fixed") %>%
    select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value) %>%
    mutate(
      estimate         = round(estimate,  5),
      std.error        = round(std.error, 5),
      statistic        = round(statistic, 5),
      p.value          = round(p.value,   5),
      climate_variable = climate_var,   # label which climate driver this model used
      trait            = trait
    )
}

# Helper: extract fixed effects from a Bayesian brms model.
# brms tidy() returns posterior mean/SD + credible interval; no z/p columns.
extract_bayes_fixed <- function(fit, climate_var, trait) {
  tidy(fit, effects = "fixed") %>%
    select(term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high) %>%
    mutate(
      estimate         = round(estimate,  5),
      std.error        = round(std.error, 5),
      conf.low         = round(conf.low,  5),
      conf.high        = round(conf.high, 5),
      climate_variable = climate_var,
      trait            = trait
    )
}


for (trait in traits) {

  # huber_value: frequentist model did not converge reliably; use the Bayesian
  # (brms) model instead so fixed-effect estimates reflect the full posterior.
  # All other traits: use the frequentist glmmTMB model.
  if (trait == "huber_value") {

    model <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_bayesian/", trait, ".RDS"))

    # Bayesian models are saved as:
    #   length 3: list(fit_MAP_stan, fit_MAT_stan, data_model)
    #             model[[1]] = precipitation (MAP), model[[2]] = temperature (MAT)
    #   length 2: list(fit_stan, data_model) — single combined model
    if (length(model) == 3) {
      fixed_tbl <- bind_rows(
        extract_bayes_fixed(model[[1]], "precipitation", trait),
        extract_bayes_fixed(model[[2]], "temperature",   trait)
      )
    } else if (length(model) == 2) {
      fixed_tbl <- extract_bayes_fixed(model[[1]], "combined", trait)
    }

  } else {

    model <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_frequentist/", trait, ".RDS"))

    # Frequentist models are saved as:
    #   length 3: list(fit_MAP, fit_MAT, data_model)
    #             model[[1]] = precipitation (MAP), model[[2]] = temperature (MAT)
    #   length 2: list(fit_lme, data_model) — single combined model
    if (length(model) == 3) {
      fixed_tbl <- bind_rows(
        extract_freq_fixed(model[[1]], "precipitation", trait),
        extract_freq_fixed(model[[2]], "temperature",   trait)
      )
    } else if (length(model) == 2) {
      fixed_tbl <- extract_freq_fixed(model[[1]], "combined", trait)
    }

  }

  doc <- read_docx()
  doc <- body_add_table(doc, value = fixed_tbl, style = "table_template")
  print(doc, target = paste0(trait, "_fixed_effects_table.docx"))
}
```


# Plot frequentist models of 2d models for plotting and coefficients - all growth forms combined, precipitation

```{r}
source("R/fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel.R")

traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)

  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    # filter(growth_form_simpler != "primitive") |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel_out_prec <- fit_model2d_frequentist_4panel(data_model, ind_variable = "log_annual_precipitation")
```

```{r}
# extract_freq_fixed / extract_bayes_fixed helpers are defined in the chunk above

traits <- unique(data_traits_climate$trait_name)
traits <- traits[seq(1:4)]

for (trait in traits) {

  # huber_value: use the Bayesian woody model for the same reason as above
  # (frequentist convergence issues); all other traits use the frequentist woody model.
  if (trait == "huber_value") {

    model <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_bayesian_woody/", trait, ".RDS"))

    # Bayesian woody models are saved as:
    #   length 3: list(fit_MAP_stan, fit_MAT_stan, data_model)
    #             model[[1]] = precipitation (MAP), model[[2]] = temperature (MAT)
    #   length 2: list(fit_stan, data_model) — single combined model
    if (length(model) == 3) {
      fixed_tbl <- bind_rows(
        extract_bayes_fixed(model[[1]], "precipitation", trait),
        extract_bayes_fixed(model[[2]], "temperature",   trait)
      )
    } else if (length(model) == 2) {
      fixed_tbl <- extract_bayes_fixed(model[[1]], "combined", trait)
    }

  } else {

    model <- readRDS(paste0("outputs/model_fits/fit2d_frequentist_woody/", trait, ".RDS"))

    # Frequentist woody models are saved as:
    #   length 3: list(fit_MAP, fit_MAT, data_model)
    #             model[[1]] = precipitation (MAP), model[[2]] = temperature (MAT)
    #   length 2: list(fit_lme, data_model) — single combined model
    if (length(model) == 3) {
      fixed_tbl <- bind_rows(
        extract_freq_fixed(model[[1]], "precipitation", trait),
        extract_freq_fixed(model[[2]], "temperature",   trait)
      )
    } else if (length(model) == 2) {
      fixed_tbl <- extract_freq_fixed(model[[1]], "combined", trait)
    }

  }

  doc <- read_docx()
  doc <- body_add_table(doc, value = fixed_tbl, style = "table_template")
  print(doc, target = paste0(trait, "_fixed_effects_table_woody.docx"))
}
```

```{r}
# For each frequentist woody fit, test whether each functional group's slope is
# different from zero (NOT whether woody differs from non-woody).
#
# Group-specific slopes:
#   non-woody = beta_base
#   woody     = beta_base + beta_interaction
#
# Test statistic for woody slope uses Var(beta_base + beta_interaction):
#   se = sqrt(Var(base) + Var(interaction) + 2*Cov(base, interaction))

woody_fit_files <- list.files(
  "outputs/model_fits/fit2d_frequentist_woody",
  pattern = "\\.RDS$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

find_interaction_term <- function(term_names, base_term) {
  cand1 <- paste0(base_term, ":woodywoody")
  cand2 <- paste0("woodywoody:", base_term)
  if (cand1 %in% term_names) return(cand1)
  if (cand2 %in% term_names) return(cand2)
  NA_character_
}

test_group_slope_zero <- function(fit, base_term, group_label) {
  term_names <- names(fixef(fit)$cond)
  vc <- as.matrix(vcov(fit)$cond)

  if (!(base_term %in% term_names)) {
    return(tibble(
      group = group_label,
      estimate = NA_real_,
      std.error = NA_real_,
      z.value = NA_real_,
      p.value = NA_real_,
      significant = NA
    ))
  }

  base_est <- unname(fixef(fit)$cond[[base_term]])

  if (group_label == "non-woody") {
    est <- base_est
    se <- sqrt(vc[base_term, base_term])
  } else {
    int_term <- find_interaction_term(term_names, base_term)
    if (is.na(int_term)) {
      est <- base_est
      se <- sqrt(vc[base_term, base_term])
    } else {
      int_est <- unname(fixef(fit)$cond[[int_term]])
      est <- base_est + int_est
      se <- sqrt(vc[base_term, base_term] + vc[int_term, int_term] + 2 * vc[base_term, int_term])
    }
  }

  z <- est / se
  p <- 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE)

  tibble(
    group = group_label,
    estimate = est,
    std.error = se,
    z.value = z,
    p.value = p,
    significant = p < 0.05
  )
}

extract_trait_slope_tests <- function(fit_obj, trait) {
  # Expected storage from fit_model2d_frequentist_woody():
  # length 3 -> list(fit_MAP, fit_MAT, data_model)
  # length 2 -> list(fit_combined, data_model) [legacy/special cases]
  if (length(fit_obj) == 3) {
    model_specs <- tribble(
      ~climate_variable, ~fit,         ~component, ~base_term,
      "precipitation",  fit_obj[[1]], "mn",      "std_log_annual_precipitation_mn",
      "precipitation",  fit_obj[[1]], "c",       "std_log_annual_precipitation_c",
      "temperature",    fit_obj[[2]], "mn",      "std_average_temperature_mn",
      "temperature",    fit_obj[[2]], "c",       "std_average_temperature_c"
    )
  } else {
    model_specs <- tribble(
      ~climate_variable, ~fit,         ~component, ~base_term,
      "precipitation",  fit_obj[[1]], "mn",      "std_log_annual_precipitation_mn",
      "precipitation",  fit_obj[[1]], "c",       "std_log_annual_precipitation_c",
      "temperature",    fit_obj[[1]], "mn",      "std_average_temperature_mn",
      "temperature",    fit_obj[[1]], "c",       "std_average_temperature_c"
    )
  }

  model_specs %>%
    mutate(
      slope_tests = pmap(
        list(fit, base_term),
        ~ bind_rows(
          test_group_slope_zero(..1, ..2, "non-woody"),
          test_group_slope_zero(..1, ..2, "woody")
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    select(-fit) %>%
    unnest(slope_tests) %>%
    mutate(
      trait = trait,
      estimate = round(estimate, 5),
      std.error = round(std.error, 5),
      z.value = round(z.value, 5),
      p.value = round(p.value, 5)
    ) %>%
    select(trait, climate_variable, component, group, estimate, std.error, z.value, p.value, significant)
}

woody_slope_zero_tables <- list()

for (fit_file in woody_fit_files) {
  trait <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(fit_file))
  fit_obj <- readRDS(fit_file)

  trait_tbl <- extract_trait_slope_tests(fit_obj, trait)
  woody_slope_zero_tables[[trait]] <- trait_tbl

  doc <- read_docx()
  doc <- body_add_table(doc, value = trait_tbl, style = "table_template")
  print(doc, target = paste0(trait, "_woody_group_slope_vs_zero_table.docx"))
}

woody_slope_zero_summary <- bind_rows(woody_slope_zero_tables)
woody_slope_zero_summary %>% View()
```

```{r}
fit_model2d_bayesian_3panel_prec_for_plot <- purrr::imap(
  fit_model2d_bayesian_3panel_prec,
  function(plot_obj, trait) {
    plot_index <- match(trait, names(fit_model2d_bayesian_3panel_prec))
    n_plots <- length(fit_model2d_bayesian_3panel_prec)

    if (plot_index != n_plots) {
      plot_obj <- plot_obj +
        theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
    }

    if (plot_index != 1) {
      plot_obj <- plot_obj +
        theme(
          strip.text = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank()
        )
    }

    plot_obj
  }
)
```
